# Rules (project-local layer)

These `.md` files are the **base rules** scaffolded into your project by `/dotclaude:init`. Claude Code loads them automatically. They extend `CLAUDE.md` without bloating it.

- `alwaysApply: true` — loaded every session. Keep tight (under ~30 lines).
- `paths: [...]` — loaded only when working near matching files.

## Ownership

Files carrying a `dotclaude:managed` marker (an HTML comment right after the frontmatter) are owned by the dotclaude base. `/dotclaude:init` overwrites them on update. To take local ownership of one, **delete its marker line** — dotclaude will then leave it alone. Any rule file you add without a marker is yours and is never touched.

The base ships: `code-quality` + `testing` (always-on), and `security`, `error-handling`, `frontend`, `database` (path-scoped). Delete the ones that don't fit your stack, or adjust their `paths:` globs.

## Adding your own

Create a new `.md` file here with `alwaysApply: true` or `paths: [...]` frontmatter. Don't add the managed marker — that signals it's yours. See [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory#path-specific-rules).
